title: Every GitLab pipeline has been 'pending' for an hour
intro: Since about 10:00 no pipeline in the shop group has started a job. They sit in 'pending'. Nobody changed any .gitlab-ci.yml. The group's jobs run on a self-hosted runner host, ci-runner-1. This morning the security team rotated 'some old CI tokens' as part of a clean-up.

steps.prompt: Start with what the pipeline says. Check the status of the current branch's pipeline.
steps.fake_output:
(pending)	test		unit
(pending)	test		lint

Pipeline state: pending
This job is stuck because the project doesn't have any runners online assigned to it.

steps.prompt: 'No runners online.' The jobs are fine; nothing is picking them up. On ci-runner-1, check whether the runner service is running.

● gitlab-runner.service - GitLab Runner

   Main PID: 1204 (gitlab-runner)

Pipeline state: running

resolution: A GitLab runner is a client: it polls the server for work, authenticating with a token it received at registration. The security clean-up removed 'old' runner registrations from the group. That invalidated the tokens in /etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml on ci-runner-1, and from that moment every poll returned 403. The runner process stayed up and looked healthy to systemd, logged errors nobody was watching, and GitLab simply had no runner for the group. Jobs don't fail in that situation; they wait, which is why this showed up as silence instead of an alert. The pipeline UI said the important thing ('no runners online'), and 'gitlab-runner verify' named the cause in one line. Registering a new runner restored service; the dead entries should also be removed from config.toml ('gitlab-runner verify --delete'). What to change afterwards. Rotations need an inventory: a token should be rotated by the team that knows where it's used, or with them, and the runner should be re-registered in the same change. Runners should be created from code (Terraform, or the Kubernetes runner chart) so that replacing one is routine and its token never lives only on a host. Monitoring should watch the queue, not the process: pending-job age and the number of online runners, both available from GitLab's API and its Prometheus metrics. And a second runner in another place means one mistake removes half the capacity instead of all of it.
